claims.claim: The semantic bridge observes game state and advertises no gameplay actions; visible UI control is a separate authority boundary.
claims.applicability: Software Inc. 1.8.41 Steam build 23094975 on the live-proven macOS x86_64 path.
limitations: Windows, native ARM64, other stores, and other game versions are unverified.

claims.claim: Pause, resume, and opening Manage Teams are live-proven visible-UI actions with fresh visual and semantic verification.
claims.applicability: Pinned English macOS build with exact-window capture and verified primary-display normalization.
limitations: Every live attempt still performs current scene, window, and target preflight.

claims.claim: Team creation, paid applicant search, and hiring are implemented and offline-tested but remain unavailable to the Guided Operator until their live mutation gate passes.
claims.applicability: Current repository Phase 4 staffing implementation.
limitations: Offline evidence is not live mutation authority.

claims.claim: A young company balances income-producing work with recurring costs while developing employee skills, teams, offices, and eventually its own products.
claims.applicability: High-level orientation only; exact optimal strategy depends on the save and observed mechanics.
limitations: The supplied guide predates the supported build and is not a current automation contract.

claims.claim: The current bridge directly observes cash and valuation, but detailed ledger, projected income, rent, and complete runway are not covered.
claims.applicability: Current read-only bridge finances coverage.
limitations: Observed cash is not a complete solvency or affordability forecast.

claims.claim: Teams group employees for work assignment and expose their name, employee count, working hours, cohesion, and compatibility in the supported observation model.
claims.applicability: Observed teams in the current company.
limitations: Observed membership does not by itself prove that a team is suitable for a particular project.

claims.claim: Creating a team is a gameplay mutation requiring an exact name, duplicate rejection, explicit approval, and semantic verification.
claims.applicability: The bounded Phase 4 create-team workflow.
limitations: Live mutation promotion remains pending.

claims.claim: The bridge completely observes current employees with stable identity, name, role, team, salary, founder state, dismissal state, and job satisfaction.
claims.applicability: Employees currently belonging to the observed company.
limitations: Current observation does not prove project suitability or future performance.

claims.claim: The initial bounded hiring workflow supports exactly one Programmer for one existing team under an explicit monthly salary ceiling.
claims.applicability: Phase 4 Low-bracket Programmer hiring slice.
limitations: Other roles, bulk hiring, benefits, specialization, and optimization are unsupported.

claims.claim: A paid applicant search and the selected employee's recurring salary are separate commitments and require separate exact approvals.
claims.applicability: Phase 4 applicant-search and hire workflow.
claims.provenance_locator: docs/adr/ADR-023 Software Inc Teams and Hiring.md
limitations: The live staffing gate has not yet promoted these commitments.

claims.claim: Employee Salary is treated by the Phase 4 observation contract as a recurring monthly payroll cost.
claims.applicability: Current Phase 4 employee and applicant observation contracts.
limitations: Complete company runway and every expense category are not observed.

claims.claim: Office readiness compares a team's observed employee count with valid, unblocked, assignable furniture that requires a chair in rooms assigned to that team; unassigned existing workstation capacity is preferred over a purchase.
claims.applicability: Player-owned indoor rooms in the current save.
limitations: The public-API workstation proxy is assignable plus needs-chair; Sim Pilot still reports the exact furniture name and does not infer that every assignable item is a desk.

claims.claim: The current bridge observes room lighting, temperature, acoustics, environment, problem counts, and furniture comfort and environment values without inventing productivity thresholds.
claims.applicability: Observed player-owned indoor rooms and furniture.
limitations: No unverified threshold is converted into a productivity claim.

claims.claim: Existing furniture exposes its one-time cost and current power draw, but exact catalog purchase price, placement, and complete recurring utility cost must be visible before Sim Pilot can request purchase approval.
claims.applicability: Current read-only office model.
limitations: Guide text alone never authorizes a purchase.

claims.claim: Each observed team exposes work start and end values; the bounded UI workflow supports whole-hour changes while paused and verifies both semantic values after applying.
claims.applicability: Current macOS 1.8.41 schedule workflow.
limitations: Fractional-hour schedules are rejected by this milestone.

claims.claim: The supported employee roles are Lead, Programmer, Designer, Artist, and Service; role changes require one exact employee and team and are verified against the employee semantic record.
claims.applicability: Current macOS 1.8.41 role workflow.
limitations: Auto-role, secondary-role optimization, and bulk changes are outside this milestone.

claims.claim: Software Inc. 1.8.41 exposes server groups, capacity, load-bearing items, power, faults, and recurring group cost, but no universal source-control server prerequisite is verified for a team.
claims.applicability: Current save server groups.
limitations: A server will only be recommended when a later selected workflow exposes a verified prerequisite.

claims.claim: The supplied Alpha 10 guide recommends an SCM server for its 2018 workflow, but that advice is historical guidance and is not treated as a current 1.8.41 automation prerequisite.
claims.applicability: Interpretation of the supplied community guide only.
limitations: The guide labels itself Alpha 10 and Steam marks it incompatible with the current game.

claims.claim: The current visible contract market identifies each job by client, software type and category, features, generated months and development time, difficulty, art ratio, minimum progress, quality target, reward, maximum penalty, and per-bug penalty. Before acceptance, generated months define a relative completion window and the public absolute deadline remains unset; after work starts, the absolute deadline is observed from the active work item. Team suitability requires observed design coverage, programming coverage when code work exists, and art coverage when art work exists. An employee assigned to Any role contributes only roles backed by observed positive skill values. Completed results expose status, bugs, gross income, net result, quality/bug/lateness penalties, and reputation change.
claims.applicability: Public ContractWork and ContractResult state in Software Inc. 1.8.41.
limitations: Public fields describe the current generated contract; they do not predict employee effectiveness or future interruptions.

claims.claim: A supported contract is selected from the completely observed visible Contracts list, assigned to an exact suitable team, accepted explicitly, advanced through its observed design and development work-item stages, promoted only when the current game exposes a valid promotion, and released only when the current game exposes a valid release.
claims.applicability: Small fixed contracts in Software Inc. 1.8.41 on the proven macOS build.
limitations: Review is performed only when an observed safe review control is available; bugs are never manufactured to satisfy a scripted count.

claims.claim: A contract is unsuitable when its reward misses the user's floor, its full observed penalty would violate the cash reserve, its generated month budget exceeds the observed time remaining, required design, programming, or art roles are missing, workspace is insufficient, or assigning the team would displace active work without approval.
claims.applicability: Deterministic first-contract recommendation policy.
limitations: The conservative estimate does not predict interruptions, effectiveness, or future expenses.

claims.claim: Contract acceptance, proceeding after observed deadline risk, review spending, promotion, and release are separately scoped commitments. Approval for one never authorizes another, and every action is rebound to the current save, session, bridge sequence, contract identity, and visible UI target.
claims.applicability: Prompt 6A operator safety boundary.
limitations: The generic persisted-task runtime remains unavailable; this is a bounded contract-specific workflow store.

claims.claim: Software Inc. 1.8.41 calls the mechanic Education. Each visible Education commitment lasts one in-game month and increases one specialization level. A three-month System-design objective therefore requires three sequential Designer/System courses from level 0 to the maximum level 3. The verified direct-cost schedule is $600, $2,000, then $5,000; the current course price is rebound to live state before every approval and click.
claims.applicability: Prompt 6B first education assignment on macOS Software Inc. 1.8.41 build 23094975.
limitations: This slice supports exactly one employee and Designer/System. An employee above level 0 cannot complete three additional courses because the specialization maximum is level 3; other education domains remain unsupported.

claims.claim: The deterministic education advisor rejects an employee already taking a course, an employee who cannot gain all three requested levels, any plan that displaces observed active work, or a projected three-course cost that violates the user's cash reserve. It reports the $7,600 level-0 curriculum cost separately from salary continuing during the three one-month absences. Every course receives a fresh exact-cost approval.
claims.applicability: Prompt 6B deterministic recommendation policy.
limitations: Continuing payroll is an indirect opportunity cost, not a second education charge; complete future cash flow is not predicted.

claims.claim: Software Inc. 1.8.41 configures a new product in the visible design window. The current read-only adapter observes the selected type and category, exact feature set and declared dependencies, available and selected operating systems, price, design and development teams, team warnings, and any selected feature server requirement before the design commitment.
prerequisites: Complete product catalog and product UI observations
claims.applicability: Prompt 7 Game Engine configuration on Software Inc. 1.8.41 build 23094975.
limitations: The old community guide does not define the current product wizard. Sim Pilot uses only fields observed from 1.8.41.

claims.claim: The verified 1.8.41 work-item model moves a product from Design to Alpha and then Beta. Alpha is the game's development phase; Sim Pilot does not invent a separate Development stage. Reviews can lead to iteration or an observed promotion, and every bounded time interval returns the game to pause. Prompt 7 stops at Beta and does not release the product.
claims.applicability: The Prompt 7 Atlas lifecycle through beta.
limitations: Release, marketing, support, sales, and revenue are reserved for Prompt 8.

claims.claim: Atlas is recommended only when Game Engine is unlocked, Core has observed design and programming capacity with no displaced active work, the exact selected configuration has no unresolved team or server prerequisite, and conservative observed payroll plus infrastructure costs keep projected cash above the user's reserve. Forecast product revenue is always zero in this calculation.
claims.applicability: Prompt 7 deterministic Atlas recommendation policy.
limitations: Unobserved future charges stop the workflow instead of being guessed.
